q: The Kurduwadi workshop in Maharashtra belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Kurduwadi workshop in Maharashtra, which handles coach and wagon work, belongs to Central Railway.

q: The Motibagh workshop at Nagpur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Motibagh workshop at Nagpur functions under South East Central Railway, headquartered at Bilaspur.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Jagadhri in Haryana belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Jagadhri in Haryana belongs to Northern Railway.

q: The Pratapnagar workshop at Vadodara, known for the maintenance of narrow gauge rolling stock, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Pratapnagar workshop at Vadodara, known for maintenance of narrow gauge rolling stock, belongs to Western Railway.

q: In railway operating statistics, the abbreviation NTKM stands for:
e: In railway operating statistics, NTKM stands for Net Tonne Kilometre, a measure of freight traffic output based on net tonnes carried multiplied by distance.

q: In Indian Railways, SRSF stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, SRSF stands for Special Railway Safety Fund, created in 2001 to wipe out arrears of track renewal and other safety works.

q: In Indian Railways, IRHS stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, IRHS stands for Indian Railway Health Service, the organised medical service of the Railways.

q: In Indian Railways, STBA stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, STBA stands for Station Ticket Booking Agent, engaged to sell unreserved tickets at small stations on commission.

q: In railway reservation rules, TDR stands for:
e: In railway reservation rules, TDR stands for Ticket Deposit Receipt, filed by a passenger to claim a refund in specified circumstances.

q: In railway stores management, AAC stands for:
e: In railway stores management, AAC stands for Average Annual Consumption, used in fixing stock limits and provisioning of stores items.

q: In Indian Railways, CCRS stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, CCRS stands for Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety, who heads the Commission of Railway Safety under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

q: In the railway accounts organisation, PFA stands for:
e: In the railway accounts organisation, PFA stands for Principal Financial Adviser, the head of the finance and accounts department of a zonal railway.

q: In railway service and pay matters, LPC stands for:
e: In railway service and pay matters, LPC stands for Last Pay Certificate, issued when an employee is transferred, recording pay and recoveries.

q: In Indian Railways, TADK stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, TADK stands for Telephone Attendant cum Dak Khalasi, the category of staff attached to officers for telephone and dak duties.

q: In departmental promotions of railway employees, LDCE stands for:
e: In departmental promotions, LDCE stands for Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, through which serving employees compete for promotion quota posts.

q: The Railway Protection Force (RPF) initiative 'Operation Seva' is primarily aimed at:

options.C: Assisting elderly, women, sick and differently-abled passengers during their journey

e: Operation Seva is an RPF initiative aimed at assisting elderly, women, sick and differently-abled passengers during their train journey.

q: Kerala's first Vande Bharat Express, flagged off in April 2023, runs between:
e: Kerala's first Vande Bharat Express, flagged off in April 2023, runs between Thiruvananthapuram and Kasaragod.

q: Kolkata's East-West Metro corridor (Howrah Maidan to Salt Lake Sector V) became fully operational in August 2025 with the inauguration of which last remaining section?
e: Kolkata's East-West Metro corridor became fully operational in August 2025 with the inauguration of the last remaining Sealdah-Esplanade section on 22 August 2025.

q: As announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, how many general non-AC coaches were planned to be manufactured over the next two to three years?
e: As announced after the Union Budget 2025-26, 17,500 general non-AC coaches were planned to be manufactured over the next two to three years, along with new Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat and Namo Bharat trains.

q: The 'Rail Rakshak Dal', a specialised rescue team for quick response at railway accident sites, was launched as a pilot project in September 2024 in which zonal railway?
e: The Rail Rakshak Dal, a specialised rescue team for quick response at accident sites, was launched as a pilot project in September 2024 in North Western Railway.

q: Chennai's first air-conditioned suburban EMU service, launched in April 2025 by Southern Railway, was introduced on which section?
e: Chennai's first air-conditioned suburban EMU service, launched by Southern Railway on 19 April 2025, was introduced on the Chennai Beach-Chengalpattu section.

q: As per the Press Information Bureau release of May 2025, how much viaduct construction had been completed on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor?
e: As per the PIB release of 20 May 2025, 300 km of viaduct construction had been completed on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor, marked by launching a 40 m girder near Surat.

q: Kavach 4.0, the upgraded version of the indigenous automatic train protection system, was first commissioned on which section of the Delhi-Mumbai route?
e: Kavach 4.0, the upgraded indigenous automatic train protection system approved by RDSO in July 2024, was first commissioned on the Mathura-Kota section of the Delhi-Mumbai route.

q: Under the first-ever India-Bhutan rail links announced in September 2025, the Samtse town of Bhutan will be connected by rail with which place in West Bengal?
e: Under the first-ever India-Bhutan rail links announced on 29 September 2025, Samtse in Bhutan will be connected with Banarhat in West Bengal by the Banarhat-Samtse line, alongside the Kokrajhar-Gelephu line.

q: The priority corridor of the Agra Metro, inaugurated in March 2024, was executed by which metro rail corporation?
e: The priority corridor of the Agra Metro, inaugurated in March 2024, was executed by Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (UPMRC).

q: The Sanskrit poem 'Meghaduta' (The Cloud Messenger), a lyric poem in which a yaksha sends a message to his beloved through a cloud, was composed by:
e: Meghaduta, the Sanskrit lyric poem in which an exiled yaksha asks a cloud to carry his message to his beloved, was composed by Kalidasa.

q: 'Kitab-ul-Hind', a celebrated account of India, its people, religion and sciences in the 11th century, was written by:
e: Kitab-ul-Hind, a detailed 11th century account of India's people, religion, sciences and customs, was written by the scholar Al-Biruni.

q: The 'Humayunnama', an account of the life and times of the Mughal emperor Humayun, was written by:
e: The Humayunnama, an account of the life and times of Emperor Humayun, was written by his sister Gulbadan Begum at Akbar's instance.

q: The 'Baburnama' (Tuzuk-i-Baburi), the memoirs of the Mughal emperor Babur, was originally written in the language:
e: The Baburnama, Babur's memoirs, was originally written in Chagatai Turkish, his mother tongue, and later translated into Persian.

q: The book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901), which put forward the 'drain of wealth' theory, was written by:
e: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901), which put forward the drain of wealth theory, was written by Dadabhai Naoroji.

q: The book 'The Indian Struggle', an account of the Indian freedom movement from 1920 to 1942, was written by:
e: The Indian Struggle, covering the freedom movement from 1920 to 1942, was written by Subhas Chandra Bose.

q: The essay 'Why I Am an Atheist', written in jail in 1930, was authored by:
e: Why I Am an Atheist was written by Bhagat Singh in jail in 1930, explaining his views on God and religion before his execution.

q: The book 'The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution' (1923) was written by:
e: The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution (1923), on Indian currency and exchange, was written by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

q: The novel 'Great Expectations', the story of the orphan Pip, was written by:
e: Great Expectations, the novel about the orphan Pip and his rise in Victorian England, was written by Charles Dickens.

q: The novel 'The Scarlet Letter', set in Puritan New England, was written by:
e: The Scarlet Letter, set in Puritan New England and centred on Hester Prynne, was written by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

q: The novel 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' (1852), a powerful work against slavery in America, was written by:
e: Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852), the influential anti-slavery novel, was written by Harriet Beecher Stowe.

q: The novel 'The Last of the Mohicans', set during the French and Indian War in North America, was written by:
e: The Last of the Mohicans, set during the French and Indian War, was written by James Fenimore Cooper as part of his Leatherstocking Tales.

q: The children's novel 'Black Beauty' (1877), narrated by a horse, was written by:
e: Black Beauty (1877), the autobiography of a horse highlighting kindness to animals, was written by Anna Sewell.

q: The children's novel 'Heidi', the story of a girl living with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps, was written by:
e: Heidi, about a girl living with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps, was written by Swiss author Johanna Spyri.

q: The novel 'Anne of Green Gables' (1908), about an orphan girl adopted on Prince Edward Island in Canada, was written by:
e: Anne of Green Gables (1908), about orphan Anne Shirley adopted on Prince Edward Island, Canada, was written by L. M. Montgomery.

q: 'The Tale of Genji', regarded as a classic of Japanese literature and often called the world's first novel, was written by:
e: The Tale of Genji, a classic of Japanese literature often called the world's first novel, was written by Lady Murasaki Shikibu in the 11th century.

q: 'The Decameron', a collection of one hundred tales told by a group of young people sheltering from the plague in Florence, was written by:
e: The Decameron, one hundred tales told over ten days by young people sheltering from the plague in Florence, was written by Giovanni Boccaccio.

q: The establishment of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) in 1982 was recommended by the:
e: The establishment of NABARD in 1982 was recommended by the Sivaraman Committee, formally the Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development (CRAFICARD).

q: The Chakravarty Committee (1985), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, was set up to review the working of the:
e: The Chakravarty Committee of 1985, appointed by the RBI under Sukhamoy Chakravarty, reviewed the working of the monetary system and recommended monetary targeting.

q: The Vaghul Committee (1987) is associated with recommendations relating to the development of the:
e: The Vaghul Committee of 1987, headed by N. Vaghul, gave recommendations for developing an integrated and efficient money market in India.

q: The States Reorganisation Commission, appointed in 1953 to examine the reorganisation of the States of India, was chaired by:
e: The States Reorganisation Commission, appointed in 1953, was chaired by Justice Fazl Ali, with H. N. Kunzru and K. M. Panikkar as members.

q: The Punchhi Commission (2007) was set up by the Government of India to examine:
e: The Punchhi Commission, set up in 2007 under Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, was constituted to examine Centre-State relations.

q: The Radhakrishnan Commission (1948-49) was appointed to inquire into and report on:
e: The Radhakrishnan Commission of 1948-49, headed by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, inquired into university education in India.

q: The Mahalanobis Committee (1960) was set up by the Government of India to study the:

options.D: Distribution of income and levels of living

e: The Mahalanobis Committee of 1960 was set up to study the distribution of income and levels of living in India during the planning era.

q: The Dutt Committee (1969) is associated with the inquiry into the:
e: The Dutt Committee of 1969, headed by Subimal Dutt, inquired into the working of the industrial licensing policy and concentration of economic power.

q: The Jain Commission, appointed in 1991, was set up to inquire into the:
e: The Jain Commission, appointed in 1991 under Justice Milap Chand Jain, inquired into the conspiracy behind the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi.

q: The Mukherjee Commission (1999) was set up to inquire into the:

options.B: Disappearance of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose

e: The Mukherjee Commission, set up in 1999 under Justice Manoj Kumar Mukherjee, inquired into the alleged disappearance of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

q: The Padmanabhaiah Committee (2000) is associated with recommendations on:
e: The Padmanabhaiah Committee of 2000, headed by K. Padmanabhaiah, is associated with recommendations on police reforms.

q: Sattriya is a classical dance form of the State of:
e: Sattriya, one of India's classical dances, originated in the monasteries (sattras) of Assam and is the classical dance form of that State.

q: Kathak is a classical dance form traditionally associated with the State of:
e: Kathak, the classical dance of storytelling through rhythmic footwork and expressions, is traditionally associated with Uttar Pradesh in northern India.

q: Durga Puja is celebrated with the greatest grandeur, with decorated pandals and idols, in the State of:
e: Durga Puja is celebrated with the greatest grandeur, with decorated pandals and idols, in West Bengal, especially in Kolkata.

q: Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated on the largest scale as a public festival in the State of:
e: Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated on the largest scale as a public festival in Maharashtra, a tradition popularised by Lokmanya Tilak.

q: The famous Rath Yatra (car festival) of Lord Jagannath is held every year at:
e: The famous Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath, with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra, is held every year at Puri in Odisha.

q: Chhath, the festival dedicated to the Sun God, is mainly celebrated in the State of:
e: Chhath, the festival dedicated to the Sun God Surya and Chhathi Maiya, is mainly celebrated in Bihar and adjoining regions.

q: A theodolite is an instrument used in surveying to measure:
e: A theodolite is a precision surveying instrument used to measure angles, both horizontal and vertical, between visible points.

q: A pedometer is an instrument used to measure the:

options.A: Number of steps taken by a person while walking

e: A pedometer is an instrument that counts the number of steps taken by a person while walking and thereby estimates distance covered.

q: A dynamometer is an instrument used to measure:
e: A dynamometer is an instrument used to measure force, torque or power, for example the power output of an engine.

q: An endoscope is a medical instrument used to:

options.A: Listen to heart and lung sounds
options.B: Examine the internal organs of the body
options.C: Measure the level of sugar in blood
options.D: Record the electrical activity of the brain

e: An endoscope is a medical instrument with a light and camera used to examine the internal organs and cavities of the body.

q: Indian Army Day is celebrated every year on:
e: Indian Army Day is celebrated on 15 January, marking the day in 1949 when General K. M. Cariappa took over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief.

q: The International Day of Yoga is observed every year on:
e: The International Day of Yoga, proposed by India and adopted by the United Nations, is observed every year on 21 June.

q: Thimphu is the capital of:
e: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.

q: Naypyidaw is the capital of:
e: Naypyidaw is the capital of Myanmar, having replaced Yangon as the administrative capital in 2005-06.

q: Tashkent is the capital of:
e: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan, the most populous country in Central Asia.

q: The national flower of India is the:
e: The lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is the national flower of India.

q: Which is the oldest mountain range in India?
e: The Aravalli Range in north-western India is the oldest mountain range in India, much older than the young fold Himalayas.

q: Haridaspur Paradip Railway Company Limited, a special purpose vehicle led by Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), was formed primarily to:

options.A: Build a new rail link between Talcher and Paradip for coal traffic
options.B: Provide an alternative broad gauge rail route between Haridaspur and Paradip Port in Odisha
options.D: Develop a multi-modal logistics park near Paradip Port

e: Haridaspur Paradip Railway Company Limited, an RVNL-led SPV, was formed to provide an alternative broad gauge rail route between Haridaspur and Paradip Port in Odisha.

q: Kinet Railway Solutions Limited, which is to manufacture Vande Bharat Sleeper trainsets at Latur in Maharashtra, is a joint venture of Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) with:
e: Kinet Railway Solutions Limited, which will manufacture Vande Bharat Sleeper trainsets at Latur, is a joint venture of RVNL with Transmashholding (TMH) of Russia and an Indian partner.

q: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), the autonomous information technology organisation of the Ministry of Railways, began functioning as a registered society in the year:
e: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), the IT organisation of the Ministry of Railways, began functioning as a registered society in 1986; it was registered in July 1986.

q: The Universal Rail Mill of the Bhilai Steel Plant of SAIL, the exclusive supplier of rails to Indian Railways, produces the world's longest single-piece rails measuring:
e: The Universal Rail Mill of SAIL's Bhilai Steel Plant produces the world's longest single-piece rails measuring 130 metres, which are welded into 260 metre panels.

q: Chennai Metro Rail Limited, which implements the Chennai Metro Rail project, is a joint venture of the Government of India and the:
e: Chennai Metro Rail Limited is a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Tamil Nadu, with equal equity participation.

q: The Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro), a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Maharashtra, is the implementing agency for the metro rail project of:
e: Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro), a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Maharashtra, is the implementing agency for the Nagpur Metro project, and also executes the Pune Metro.

q: The Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (UPMRC), which executes metro projects in cities like Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra, was earlier known as the:
e: Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (UPMRC), which executes metro projects in Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra, was earlier known as Lucknow Metro Rail Corporation.

q: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) was incorporated under the Companies Act in the year:
e: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) was incorporated on 3 May 1995 under the Companies Act, with equal equity of the Government of India and the Government of Delhi.

q: BEML Limited, which manufactures metro coaches and Vande Bharat trainsets, is a public sector undertaking under the administrative control of the:

options.D: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

e: BEML Limited, which manufactures metro coaches and Vande Bharat trainsets, is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Defence.

q: The wagon manufacturing unit at Kulti in West Bengal, set up as the SAIL RITES Bengal Wagon Industry Private Limited, is a joint venture of RITES Limited with:
e: The wagon unit at Kulti in West Bengal, SAIL RITES Bengal Wagon Industry Private Limited, is a joint venture of RITES Limited with Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

q: Ircon Renewable Power Limited, a joint venture of Ircon International Limited with Ayana Renewable Power, was incorporated for setting up:

options.A: Rooftop solar plants on railway stations
options.B: A 100 MW wind power project in Tamil Nadu
options.C: A 500 MW grid-connected solar power plant under the CPSU Scheme Phase-II

e: Ircon Renewable Power Limited, a joint venture of Ircon International with Ayana Renewable Power, was incorporated for setting up a 500 MW grid-connected solar power plant under the CPSU Scheme Phase-II.

q: In the Kerala Rail Development Corporation Limited (K-Rail), which has taken up the SilverLine semi-high speed rail project, the majority equity of 51 per cent is held by the:
e: In Kerala Rail Development Corporation Limited (K-Rail), which has taken up the SilverLine semi-high speed project, the Government of Kerala holds the majority equity of 51 per cent.

q: Punjab Logistics Infrastructure Limited, a joint venture of CONCOR with the Punjab State Container and Warehousing Corporation (CONWARE), has set up its Multi Modal Logistics Park at:
e: Punjab Logistics Infrastructure Limited, a joint venture of CONCOR with Punjab State Container and Warehousing Corporation (CONWARE), has set up its Multi Modal Logistics Park at Ahmedgarh in Ludhiana district.

q: The Patna Metro Rail Corporation Limited, the special purpose vehicle implementing the Patna Metro Rail project, is a joint venture of the Government of India with the Government of:
e: Patna Metro Rail Corporation Limited, the SPV implementing the Patna Metro, is a joint venture of the Government of India with the Government of Bihar.

q: Besides the Kochi Metro, the Kochi Metro Rail Limited also operates which other public transport system launched in Kochi in 2023?
e: Besides the Kochi Metro, Kochi Metro Rail Limited also operates the Kochi Water Metro, the water-based public transport system launched in Kochi in 2023.

q: The Northern Railway was created in April 1952 by amalgamating the Eastern Punjab Railway and the Jodhpur and Bikaner State Railways with three divisions of the:
e: Northern Railway was created in April 1952 by amalgamating the Eastern Punjab Railway and the Jodhpur and Bikaner State Railways with three divisions of the East Indian Railway.

q: The South Central Railway, formed by merging the Hubballi division of Southern Railway with the Secunderabad division of Central Railway, came into existence in the year:
e: South Central Railway, formed by merging the Hubballi division of Southern Railway with the Secunderabad division of Central Railway, came into existence in 1966.

q: The East Central Railway, with headquarters at Hajipur, was formed by carving out divisions from which two zonal railways?

options.A: Eastern Railway and South Eastern Railway
options.B: North Eastern Railway and Northeast Frontier Railway
options.C: Eastern Railway and North Eastern Railway

e: East Central Railway, headquartered at Hajipur, was formed by carving out divisions from Eastern Railway and North Eastern Railway.

q: The Central Railway, formed around the nucleus of the Great Indian Peninsula Railway, came into existence in the year:
e: Central Railway, formed around the nucleus of the Great Indian Peninsula Railway, came into existence on 5 November 1951.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Hubballi, one of the major workshops of Indian Railways, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Hubballi functions under South Western Railway, which is headquartered at Hubballi.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Lalgarh, Bikaner, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Lalgarh, Bikaner, functions under North Western Railway.

q: The Wagon Workshop at Rayanapadu, near Vijayawada, which undertakes periodic overhaul of freight wagons, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Wagon Workshop at Rayanapadu, near Vijayawada, which undertakes periodic overhaul of freight wagons, functions under South Central Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Erode, which homed WAP class electric locomotives, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Erode, which homed WAP class electric locomotives, functions under Southern Railway.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Vatva, Ahmedabad, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Vatva, Ahmedabad, functions under Western Railway.

q: The railway workshop at Dibrugarh in Assam, one of the oldest workshops of Indian Railways, was established in the year:
e: The railway workshop at Dibrugarh in Assam, one of the oldest workshops of Indian Railways, was established in 1881, as recorded in Northeast Frontier Railway's history of Tinsukia division.

q: The first steam locomotive turned out by the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works in November 1950 was named:
e: The first steam locomotive turned out by Chittaranjan Locomotive Works in November 1950 was named Deshbandhu, after Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das.

q: The first diesel-electric locomotive rolled out by the Diesel Locomotive Works at Varanasi in January 1964 was named:
e: The first diesel-electric locomotive rolled out by Diesel Locomotive Works, Varanasi in January 1964, a WDM-2 built from an ALCo kit and flagged off on 3 January 1964, was named Kundan.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'UTS', used for issuing unreserved tickets at stations, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, UTS stands for Unreserved Ticketing System, the computer application used for issuing unreserved tickets at stations.

q: In Indian Railways, the computerised reservation application 'PRS' stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, PRS stands for Passenger Reservation System, the computerised application that handles reserved ticketing across the network.

q: In railway train operations, the document 'WTT', which lays down the scheduled timings of trains for official use, stands for:
e: In railway train operations, WTT stands for Working Time Table, the official document laying down scheduled timings of trains for departmental use.
